rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, nor refuse to rent, terminate, or demand higher deposits or rent based on it. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages of actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.status_basis: Berkeley City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020.

exempt_if.text: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

exempt_if.name: owner_move_back_rental_agreement
exempt_if.text: Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9

exempt_if.name: existing_tenant_sublet_roommate
exempt_if.text: Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley regarding current and prospective tenants.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 cases, owner move-back agreements, and existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.

rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
